items.text: Format: return CSV text. The first row is the header id,title,owner,amount; then one row per exported record, in ascending id order, with those four fields. Produce it with Python's csv.writer (default dialect) and lineterminator='\n'. With no exported records, return the header row alone (ending in '\n').
Viewers: if user['role'] is 'viewer', raise PermissionError; nothing is exported.
Scope: a user whose role is 'admin' may export records of any project. Any other role exports only records whose 'project' is in user['projects']; other records are left out without an error.
Status: only records with status 'active' are exported, unless params.get('include_archived') is True; then records with status 'archived' are exported too.

Confidential records: a record whose 'confidential' is True is never exported, with one exception: it is exported when user['role'] is 'admin' and params.get('purpose') == 'audit'. Every other rule still applies to it.
Decision record: CSV was chosen for the first release because the finance team imports exports into spreadsheets.
Date filter: params may contain 'since', a date string 'YYYY-MM-DD'. When it is present, only records whose 'created' date is on or after that date are exported.
Residency: a record whose 'region' is 'eu' is exported only when 'eu' is in user['regions']; this applies to admins too.
Record limit: params may contain 'max_records', an int of at least 1. Export only the first max_records records, in ascending id order, that remain after every other rule.

Compliance obligation (nothing to do while the format is CSV): if a later stage changes the export format from CSV, every export in the new format must include a top-level field "exported_by" equal to user['name']. It stays in force unless a later stage withdraws or changes it.
Titles: export each record's title with leading and trailing whitespace removed.

Audit-trail obligation (nothing to do today): if confidential records are ever exported for a purpose other than 'audit', every such export must include a top-level field "confidential_count" giving the number of confidential records it contains.

Exports are now JSON text (json.dumps) of an object whose key "records" lists one object per exported record, in ascending id order, with exactly the keys "id" (int), "title", "owner" and "amount" (str, exactly as given). The hidden tests parse the JSON and compare values, not spacing or key order.
Users whose role is neither 'admin' nor 'viewer' may now also export the records they own (record 'owner' equal to user['name']), even outside their projects.
For information: storage for archived projects moves to a cheaper tier next quarter. This does not change what exports contain.
include_archived is now honoured only when user['role'] is 'admin'; for every other role, archived records are never exported.
Region values may now be written in upper or lower case, in records and in user['regions']; compare region values case-insensitively.
Titles: in addition, replace every run of whitespace inside a title with a single space.
Confidential records may now also be exported when user['role'] is 'admin' and params.get('purpose') == 'legal'.
Viewers no longer receive an error: a viewer now exports only the records they own (record 'owner' equal to user['name']), in any project; every other rule still applies to those records.
Decision record: the move to JSON was made for the new reporting API.
The "exported_by" field is no longer required when user['role'] is 'admin'; admin exports omit it.
A max_records value above 30 is treated as 30.
For information: the web interface now shows 50 records per page. This does not change exports.
Each exported JSON record now also has the key "project" (the record's project).
The residency restriction is withdrawn: records of every region are exported under the ordinary rules.
For information: the security team confirmed that this notice does not change the confidential-record rules.
